meta.title: A timed WNT pulse doubles mature enterocytes in human intestinal organoids
meta.reviewed: Written by hand from source/manuscript.md: the lab-notebook figure style (warm paper, light grid, brightfield with phase halos, Literata and a monospaced face) is the look; the four panels are the scenes.

source.notes: fictional stem-cell article: abstract, Figure 1 legend (a-d), notebook style
Literata and Spline Sans Mono (SIL OFL 1.1)

rationale.palette: Notebook paper (#F4EFE4) with a faint blue grid, brightfield greys for the images (#D9D4CA field, #6E665C cell walls, white phase halos), and the stains only where the figure uses them: villin magenta (#C2185B) and LGR5 green (#2E7D32). Pencil graphite for annotations.
rationale.type: Literata for sentences and margin notes (the 'handwritten-feeling serif'), Spline Sans Mono for days, doses and well IDs.
rationale.motion: Time-lapse patience: the organoid grows continuously with a day counter, buds push out, notes are written in as the days pass; the plate fills well by well. Ease ioSine, no hits.
rationale.sound: Bench-side warmth: corporate preset at 100 BPM in D major with marimba and soft strings, light drums.
rationale.visuals: A Matrigel dome with seeded stem cells, the brightfield time-lapse from one cell to a budding organoid, the protocol timeline with the 96-well plate map, and the day-7 result with a villin-stained organoid.
